content.title: Learning Objective
content.description: Master the fundamental operations on arrays including traversal, insertion, deletion, updating elements, and analyzing their time complexities.

content.content: Arrays are among the most widely used data structures because they provide fast indexed access and store elements in contiguous memory locations. Understanding basic array operations is essential before moving to advanced data structures.

content.title: Where Are Arrays Used?
content.content: Arrays are used internally in matrices, heaps, dynamic arrays, strings, image processing, databases, and operating systems.

content.definition: Traversal is the process of visiting every element of an array exactly once for performing operations such as printing, searching, updating, or calculating.

content.content: Traversal begins from the first index (0) and continues until the last index (n-1). Every element is processed sequentially.

content.title: Array Traversal

content.content: Accessing an element using its index is the fastest operation in arrays because memory addresses are calculated directly.

content.title: Why Access is Fast
content.content: Memory Address = Base Address + (Index × Size of Element). This calculation takes constant time.

content.definition: Insertion adds a new element into the array. Existing elements must shift whenever insertion happens in the middle.

content.content: If an element is inserted anywhere except the last position, all subsequent elements shift one position toward the right.

content.title: Insertion Cost
content.content: Insertion near the beginning of an array is expensive because many elements need to be shifted.

content.definition: Deletion removes an element from the array and shifts the remaining elements left to fill the gap.

content.content: Deleting an element from the middle requires shifting all subsequent elements to maintain contiguous memory.

content.title: Deletion Cost
content.content: Deletion is efficient only at the end of the array. Removing elements from the middle requires shifting.
Updating means replacing the value stored at a specific index. Since the address is already known, updating happens instantly.

content.title: Books on a Shelf
content.description: Imagine books arranged neatly on a shelf. Reading any book is easy if you know its position. Adding or removing a book from the middle requires shifting the remaining books.

items.question: Why is array access O(1)?
items.answer: Because the memory address is calculated directly using the index.

items.question: Why are insertion and deletion O(n)?
items.answer: Because elements need to shift to maintain contiguous memory.

items.question: Is traversal always O(n)?
items.answer: Yes, because every element must be visited.

content.title: Did You Know?
content.content: Most programming languages internally implement strings, vectors, and dynamic arrays using contiguous memory similar to arrays.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Interviewers often ask why insertion and deletion are slow in arrays. Always explain contiguous memory and element shifting.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Arrays store elements in contiguous memory.
Arrays are best when fast random access is required.
